title: BECE English Studies: Grammar & Structure - English Studies - Parts of Speech - Pronouns
subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate relative pronoun:
"The girl _____ won the scholarship is my cousin."
questions.explain: The pronoun 'who' is used as the subject of a relative clause referring to people. In the relative clause '_____ won the scholarship', the subject is missing, so 'who' is the correct choice.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the correct pronoun:
"Between you and _____, I don't think this plan will work."
questions.explain: The preposition 'between' requires an object pronoun. While 'you and I' is commonly mistakenly used, 'you and me' is grammatically correct because 'me' is the object form.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate reflexive pronoun:
"The president _____ delivered the opening address."
questions.explain: Here, 'himself' acts as an intensive pronoun to emphasize the noun 'The president'. 'Hisself' is not a valid word in standard English grammar.
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun:
"This is the boy _____ father is a renowned surgeon."
questions.explain: The relative pronoun 'whose' shows possession. It correctly links the boy to his father, meaning 'the father of the boy'.
